description: 'Iron Goddess of Mercy'. One of China's most famous oolongs, with two distinct processing styles.
historical_background: Legend tells of a devout farmer who was gifted the plant in a dream by the Bodhisattva Guanyin. The cultivar is technically known as 'Hong Xin Wai Wei Tao' (Red Heart Crooked Tail Peach).

description: 'Original Mountain'. A close relative of Tie Guan Yin, often used as a more affordable alternative or blender.
historical_background: Grown in the mountains neighboring Anxi, it is genetically similar to Tie Guan Yin but produces a lighter-bodied tea.

description: 'Hairy Crab'. An Anxi oolong cultivar named for the downy hairs on its leaves.
historical_background: Named for the fine white hairs (down) on its leaves and the shape of the brewed leaf. It is a productive and fragrant cultivar.

description: 'Big Red Robe', the most famous Wuyi Rock Oolong. Most modern DHP is a blend, but the name refers to legendary mother trees.
historical_background: Legend says the tea cured an emperor's mother, who then draped her red robes over the bushes in gratitude. The original 6 mother trees are a national treasure.

description: 'Cassia/Cinnamon'. A top-tier Wuyi Rock Oolong prized for its pronounced spicy aroma. One of the most popular Yancha cultivars today.
historical_background: Originally from a different area, it was found to thrive in Wuyi's rocky terroir, becoming a star cultivar.

description: 'Water Sprite' or 'Narcissus'. A versatile and common Wuyi Rock Oolong cultivar, prized for its woody depth, especially from old groves (Lao Cong).
historical_background: Originally from Southern Fujian, it was transplanted to Wuyi where it developed a unique character. 'Lao Cong' (old grove) Shui Xian is highly sought after.
growth_habits: Can grow into a small tree (arbor)

description: 'Iron Arhat'. One of the four great historical Wuyi cultivars, known for its powerful character and medicinal notes.
historical_background: One of the oldest named Wuyi cultivars, fabled to have been discovered by a powerful monk (Arhat).

description: 'White Cockscomb'. A unique Wuyi cultivar with pale, yellowish leaves, processed with a lighter roast.
historical_background: Named for the unique pale color and shape of its leaves. It's an outlier among Yancha for its light oxidation and roast.

description: 'Golden Water Turtle'. Another of the four great Wuyi cultivars, known for a vibrant and lasting floral fragrance.
historical_background: Legend says the original bush was washed by a flood from its monastery home to a new location, hence the name.

description: 'Half-way to the Sky'. A famous Wuyi cultivar named because the original bush grew halfway up a cliff face.
historical_background: A classic and elegant Yancha, known for being perfectly balanced and representative of the Wuyi character without extreme notes.

description: 'Yellow Goddess'. A modern hybrid of Tie Guan Yin and Huang Jin Gui, bred for exceptionally high fragrance.
historical_background: A successful modern cultivar that combines the aroma of its parents and adapts it to the Wuyi terroir, resulting in a powerfully fragrant Yancha.

description: 'Golden Osmanthus'. An Anxi Oolong known for its extremely fragrant, almost perfume-like aroma.
historical_background: Named for its golden liquor color and intense osmanthus flower aroma. It is an early-budding cultivar.

description: 'Fuding Big White', the premier cultivar for producing high-grade white teas like Silver Needle.
historical_background: Selected and propagated in the Fuding area for its exceptionally large, downy buds, becoming the gold standard for white tea production.
processing_suitability: light green leaves covered in dense white down (hao)

description: 'Zhenghe Big White'. Another key white tea cultivar, known for producing a fuller-bodied tea than its Fuding counterpart.
historical_background: Developed in the Zhenghe region, it has slightly smaller buds than Fuding Da Bai and is also used for black tea production (e.g., Panyong Congou).
leaf_characteristics: Slightly smaller leaves than Fuding Da Bai

description: 'Wuyi Vegetable Tea'. The local heirloom seed-grown population, and the original cultivar for Lapsang Souchong.
historical_background: This is the native, genetically diverse small-leaf population of the Wuyi region, predating all the named clonal cultivars.

description: 'Honey Orchid Fragrance'. The most popular and representative Dan Cong oolong, known for its intoxicating aroma.
historical_background: A specific fragrance-type selected from the local Shui Xian population in the Phoenix Mountains, bred to mimic the scent of honey and orchids.

description: 'Duck Shit Fragrance'. Famously misnamed, this Dan Cong is celebrated for its creamy texture and gardenia aroma.
historical_background: Legend says a farmer gave it an ugly name to deter theft. Now often marketed as 'Yin Hua Xiang' (Honeysuckle Fragrance).

description: 'Almond Fragrance'. A classic Dan Cong fragrance type known for its distinct nutty, marzipan-like aroma.
historical_background: One of the ten traditional fragrance types of Dan Cong, selected for its unique nutty aromatic profile.

description: 'Orchid Fragrance'. A classic Dan Cong prized for its elegant, refined, and high-pitched orchid notes.
historical_background: Considered one of the most elegant and classic Dan Cong profiles, it is a benchmark for floral aroma.

description: 'Song Dynasty Cultivar'. Descendants of the oldest known tea tree on Wudong Mountain, the apex of Dan Cong oolongs.
historical_background: Refers to tea made from the direct descendants of a tree said to be over 600 years old. Very rare and prized for its depth and power.

description: 'Eight Immortals'. A clonal Dan Cong cultivar known for its very strong, assertive fragrance and powerful character.
historical_background: A clonal cultivar developed from eight cuttings of a Song Zhong tree, hence the name. It is known for its intense aroma.

description: The most widespread modern clone for producing West Lake Long Jing. Prized for its early budding, beautiful appearance, and high yield.
historical_background: Developed by the Tea Research Institute of the Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences from the local Long Jing Qunti population to standardize and improve yield.

description: The original, heirloom 'population' of mixed Long Jing cultivars, propagated by seed. Considered more complex by connoisseurs.
historical_background: This is the original genetic pool of West Lake Long Jing before modern clonal selection. It has greater biodiversity and a later harvest time than #43.
growth_habits: Variable growth due to genetic diversity

description: 'Anji White Tea', a green tea cultivar whose leaves turn a pale, whitish-green in early spring, yielding a tea high in amino acids.
historical_background: A rare mutation where low spring temperatures inhibit chlorophyll production. It is processed as a green tea despite its name.
harvest_seasons: almost white leaves in early spring

description: The local heirloom population for Bi Luo Chun green tea, known for its intense fruitiness and delicate, downy leaves.
historical_background: Camellia sinensis var. sinensis
growth_habits: The original small-leaf, seed-propagated population from the Dongting mountains, traditionally intercropped with fruit trees.

description: The local heirloom population of Huangshan (Yellow Mountain), used for the famous Huangshan Maofeng green tea.
historical_background: Camellia sinensis var. sinensis
growth_habits: The native, seed-grown population of the Yellow Mountain scenic area, known for its sweet and floral character.

description: 'Persimmon Big Tea'. A unique, massive-leaf cultivar used exclusively for making Tai Ping Hou Kui green tea.
historical_background: Camellia sinensis var. sinensis
growth_habits: A unique large-leaf cultivar local to Taiping county, which produces visually stunning, long, flat leaves when processed.

description: 'Big Leaf Variety'. This refers to the broad-leaf varietal, C. sinensis var. assamica, the genetic backbone of all Yunnan tea.
historical_background: The ancestor of all tea, this varietal is native to the region encompassing Yunnan, Myanmar, and Assam, India.
growth_habits: Can grow into a large tree

description: 'Purple Juan'. A modern Yunnan cultivar developed from a natural purple-leaf mutation, very high in anthocyanins.
historical_background: Developed at the Yunnan Tea Research Institute from a purple-leaf mutation for its unique chemical composition and striking appearance.
harvest_seasons: and stems are a deep purple color

description: 'Qimen Species'. The local heirloom population used for all Keemun black teas, famous for its complex aroma.
historical_background: These are the local small-leaf cultivars that, when processed into black tea using newly learned techniques in the 1870s, yielded the unique 'Keemun fragrance'.
leaf_characteristics: Variable due to being a population

description: 'Green Heart'. The quintessential cultivar for Taiwanese high mountain oolongs, prized for its ability to express terroir.
historical_background: Brought from Fujian, China, it became the most valued cultivar in Taiwan for its elegant character, especially when grown at high altitudes.

description: 'Golden Lily'. A modern TRES-bred cultivar famous for its distinct, natural milky fragrance.
historical_background: Developed by the Taiwan Tea Research and Extension Station (TRES), it was a massive success due to its unique flavor profile and high yield.

description: 'Four Seasons Spring'. A prolific cultivar known for its explosive floral aroma, harvestable almost year-round.
historical_background: A natural cross found by a farmer in the Muzha area. Its productivity and strong aroma made it commercially successful.

description: 'Green Heart Big Hairy'. The primary cultivar for Oriental Beauty oolong, requiring bites from a specific insect to develop its flavor.
historical_background: Camellia sinensis var. sinensis
growth_habits: A relative of Qing Xin Oolong, this cultivar responds perfectly to the bites of the tea leafhopper (Jacobiasca formosana), creating a unique honey fragrance.
harvest_seasons: Slightly larger and hairier leaves than Qing Xin

description: 'Jade'. A TRES-bred cultivar known for a powerful floral aroma, often compared to magnolia.
historical_background: Released alongside Jin Xuan, it's another high-yield, aromatic cultivar, though generally considered crisper and more purely floral than its sibling.
leaf_characteristics: Slightly more pointed leaves than Jin Xuan

description: 'Ruby'. A famous TRES-bred hybrid, creating Taiwan's most unique black tea.
scientific_name: C. sinensis var. assamica x C. formosensis
historical_background: A hybrid of a native Taiwanese wild tea tree (C. formosensis) and a Burmese Assamica varietal. Bred specifically for black tea.

description: 'Red Rhyme'. A modern TRES-bred black tea cultivar with a distinct citrusy and floral character.
historical_background: A hybrid between an Indian 'Kyang' variety and a Keemun cultivar, designed to produce a highly aromatic black tea.
leaf_characteristics: a bit smaller than Hong Yu

description: 'Buddha's Hand'. A large-leaf cultivar grown in both Fujian and Taiwan, known for its thick body and fruity notes.
historical_background: Camellia sinensis var. sinensis
growth_habits: The same cultivar as from Fujian, but it expresses itself differently in Taiwan's terroir and with local processing styles.

description: 'Welcome Fragrance'. A new-generation TRES cultivar bred for a powerful and elegant floral aroma.
historical_background: A modern cultivar designed to have the elegance of Qing Xin but with a more intense, tropical floral character. A promising new release.

description: 'White Hairs'. A modern TRES cultivar bred specifically for making leafhopper-bitten teas like Oriental Beauty.
historical_background: Camellia sinensis var. sinensis
growth_habits: Developed as a more pest-resistant and productive alternative to Qing Xin Da Mao for producing high-quality honey-fragrance teas.
image_url: a bit larger than Qing Xin Da Mao

description: The native Taiwanese wild tea species, genetically distinct from C. sinensis. Used in breeding and for specialty wild-harvested teas.
historical_background: The indigenous tea species of Taiwan. It is the genetic parent of Hong Yu #18 and is valued for its unique, wild character.

description: The undisputed king of Japanese tea, accounting for ~75% of all production. It is the benchmark for classic Sencha flavor.
historical_background: Discovered by Hikosaburo Sugiyama in a bamboo grove ('Yabu'). Registered in 1953, its balance and hardiness led to its nationwide dominance.

name_native: ゆたかみどり / 豊緑
description: 'Abundant Green'. An early-budding cultivar, very popular in the warmer Kagoshima region, especially for deep-steamed Sencha.
historical_background: An early-budding cultivar that became popular in southern Japan for its high yield and suitability for deep-steaming, which reduces its natural astringency.

description: 'Clear Green'. A modern elite cultivar prized for its vibrant color and low bitterness. A hybrid of Yabukita and Asatsuyu.
historical_background: Bred for superior color and a sweeter, umami-rich profile. Often used in competition-grade teas.

description: 'Late Green'. A late-budding, versatile cultivar with a rich, creamy flavor, often used for Matcha or blended with Yabukita.
historical_background: A hybrid of Yabukita and a Zairai, it is harvested after Yabukita, extending the harvest season. Its balanced profile makes it a superb blender.

description: 'Enlightenment'. A classic, elite Uji cultivar bred specifically for shaded teas like Gyokuro and Matcha.
historical_background: An old, traditional Uji cultivar selected for its exceptional response to shading, creating the archetypal deep umami flavor of Gyokuro.

name_native: うじひかり / 宇治光
description: 'Light of Uji'. A premier Uji cultivar for high-grade Gyokuro and Matcha, known for its elegant character and bright color.
historical_background: Another elite cultivar from Uji's breeding programs, selected for its refined aroma and brilliant green liquor.

description: A foundational Uji cultivar, widely used for high-grade Matcha due to its excellent color and balanced flavor.
historical_background: One of the core Uji cultivars that has been a workhorse for the Matcha industry for decades.

description: 'Morning Sun'. A top-tier Uji cultivar used for the highest grades of ceremonial Matcha.
historical_background: An old, elite Uji cultivar prized for its supremely elegant and sweet umami profile, with almost no bitterness.

description: 'Fragrance of Shizuoka'. A modern cultivar bred specifically for its astonishingly powerful floral and fruity aroma.
historical_background: Bred from 'Kurizawa' and 'Kanayamidori', its unique aroma profile makes it a standout for modern, fragrant Senchas and Japanese oolongs.

description: 'Blue Wind'. A modern aromatic cultivar known for its striking, almost perfume-like aroma of black currant and mint.
historical_background: Another modern aromatic cultivar, often used for unique Senchas or lightly oxidized Japanese oolongs.

description: 'Late Light'. A late-budding cultivar with a refreshing, brisk mouthfeel and a distinct floral and woody character.
historical_background: A versatile late-harvest cultivar that provides a unique flavor profile different from the main Sencha types.

description: A classic cultivar specific to the Kamairicha-producing regions of Kyushu, known for its excellent pan-fired character.
historical_background: A traditional cultivar selected for its ability to withstand pan-firing, producing a signature nutty and roasted aroma (kama-ka).

name_native: べにふうき / 紅富貴
description: 'Red Riches'. Japan's most famous black tea cultivar, a hybrid of Assamica varieties.
historical_background: Bred from 'Benihomare' and a Darjeeling-lineage parent. Also famous for high levels of methylated catechins, studied for anti-allergy effects.

name_native: べにひかり / 紅ひかり
description: 'Red Light'. A classic Japanese black tea cultivar with Darjeeling lineage, known for its muscatel-like aroma.
historical_background: An earlier black tea hybrid, it is more aromatic and less astringent than Benifuki, often compared to a second-flush Darjeeling.

description: 'Conventional'. The term for any un-cloned, seed-propagated heirloom tea bush population in Japan, representing pre-modern tea genetics.
historical_background: Before the development of clonal cultivars, all Japanese tea came from Zairai fields. They possess huge genetic diversity and regional character.
growth_habits: Highly variable; bushes grow differently from seed
